# UK coal productivity and production statistics, 1700 to 2025?

UK coal production ramped from 4MTpa in 1700, to 17MTpa in 1800, had surpassed 100MTpa by 1870, had surpassed 200MTpa by 1900, peaked at 290MTpa in 1913, then declined steadily towards zero by 2025. In this data-file we have tabulated very long-term UK coal productivity and production statistics.

Genuine energy transitions, where one form of energy is displaced by another, are relatively few in number. We have previously studied the rise and fall of whale oil.

However the rise and fall of UK coal may hold lessons for other resources globally, such as the maturation of Chinese coal within China’s energy market, or possibly the eventual maturation of US shale.

In this data-file, first we chart the rise of coal from the medieval era through to the middle of the industrial revolution, which did not displace wood but more accurately, “layered in on top” (charts below).

UK coal production peaked at 290MTpa in 1913, prior to World War I. Our main goal in this data-file is to see how costs and productivity metrics evolved as UK coal production declined.

Data sources used in the file include the UK Department of Energy and Climate Change, academic papers, and disclosures from the UK’s National Coal Board, from 1947 to 1987.

UK coal production from 1870 to 2025, and UK coal consumption from 1870 to 2025 are available, albeit with some interpolation in early years.

UK coal production data by region are available intermittently from 1952 to 1966, across Yorkshire, the Midlands, the North West, South West, Northumberland and Scotland.

The number of collieries in operation is available annually, declining from 3,000 in 1913 to zero in 2025. From this, we can also estimate the average coal production per mine (in kTpa).

The number of employees in the UK coal industry is available annually, from 1875 to 2025, and from this we can estimate the labor productivity of UK coal production by year from 1875 to 2025.

Mechanization in the coal industry is available by counting the number of coal-cutting machines (1903-1915), the percent of coal that is mechanically cut, conveyed and loaded (1947-1966), the types of supports used in the industry (1951 to 1967) and the electric horsepower per man (1947-1966).

Capital expenditure across the entire UK coal industry is estimated from 1920 to 1981, albeit the data are patchy in the early years. We have converted the numbers into $2025 for comparability.

Total production costs across the entire UK coal industry are estimated at periodic intervals from 1938 to 1966. We have converted the numbers into $2025 for comparability.

Accident rates and fatality rates across the entire UK coal industry are available annually from 1947 to 1966.

Please message us if we can help you expand this data-file and find missing data-points.

This data-file was last updated on 05-Nov-26.
